definition: An equation that contains a derivative, such as $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2y$; solving it means finding the function.
The family of all solutions of a differential equation, written with an arbitrary constant.
The one solution of a differential equation that fits a given condition, such as a known point on the curve.
The differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d}n}{\mathrm{d}t} = kn(a - n)$, whose solutions grow and then level off towards $a$.
A first-order differential equation that can be written as $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = f\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)$, solved with the substitution $y = vx$.
The multiplier $\mathrm{e}^{\int P(x)\,\mathrm{d}x}$ that turns the left side of $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + P(x)y = Q(x)$ into the derivative of one product.
A numerical method that estimates a solution of $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = f(x, y)$ by repeated short steps along the tangent.
